subject: Banking
title: Why Banks Love Checking Accounts
description: A 60-second lesson on Why Banks Love Checking Accounts.

hook.text: Checking accounts pay zero interest. Banks lend that money at 7%. Free deposits are the most profitable funding source.

buildup.text: Banks call non-interest-bearing deposits 'core deposits.' They're stable, free.

discovery.text: JPMorgan has $2.4 trillion in deposits. A large share paying zero interest generates billions in free lending capital.

twist.text: Banks spend heavily on free checking perks to attract these deposits.

climax.text: Free checking isn't charity. It's the cheapest funding a bank can get, and they would spend a lot to keep it.

punchline.text: Free checking pays the bank, not you. Zero-interest deposits are pure profit.

quiz.question: Why do banks offer free checking accounts?
options: Zero-interest deposits are the cheapest source of lending capital
